result.topic_en: An outline for presenting Newton's theorem on the sums of powers of the roots of equations, starting from the factorization of a polynomial into linear factors and forming differences of the generating products in two variables t and u.
result.transcription:
Math 20
[-45b/15-] (14)

Vortrag des Newtonschen Lehrsatzes
über die Summen der Potenzen
der Wurzeln der Gleichungen.

1) Wenn $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$ u.s.w. die Wurzeln der Gleichung
$x^m + Px^{m-1} + Qx^{m-2} + Rx^{m-3} + \text{etc.} + Tx + U = 0$
sind so ist
$x^m + Px^{m-1} + Qx^{m-2} + Rx^{m-3} + \text{etc.}$
das Product aus den einfachen Factoren $x-\alpha, x-\beta, x-\gamma, x-\delta$ &c.
2) Zusammenhang der Coefficienten $P, Q, R$ &c. mit den Wurzeln
3) Man hat dann auch
$1 + Pt + Qt^2 + Rt^3 + \&c. + Tt^{m-1} + Ut^m$
$= (1-\alpha t)(1-\beta t)(1-\gamma t)(1-\delta t)$ etc.
4) [-Man setze-] Die Differenz
$1 + Pt + Qtt + Rt^3 + \&c + Tt^{m-1} + Ut^m$
$-(1 + Pu + Quu + Ru^3 + \&c. + Tu^{m-1} + Uu^m)$
ist $= (t-u)(P + Q(t+u) + R(t^2+tu+uu) + \text{etc.})$
5) Die Differenz $(1-\alpha t)(1-\beta t)(1-\gamma t)(1-\delta t) \ldots$
$- (1-\alpha u)(1-\beta u)(1-\gamma u)(1-\delta u) \ldots$
ist $= (u-t)\alpha(1-\beta t)(1-\gamma t)(1-\delta t) \ldots$
$+ (u-t)\beta(1-\alpha u)(1-\gamma t)(1-\delta t) \ldots$
$+ (u-t)\gamma(1-\alpha u)(1-\beta u)(1-\delta t) \ldots$
$+ (u-t)\delta(1-\alpha u)(1-\beta u)(1-\gamma u) \ldots$
$+$ &c.

methods.what: Factorization of a monic polynomial into linear factors given its roots
methods.quote: das Product aus den einfachen Factoren $x-\alpha, x-\beta, x-\gamma, x-\delta$ &c.

methods.what: Reversed polynomial factorization (generating function in t)
methods.quote:
$1 + Pt + Qt^2 + Rt^3 + \&c. + Tt^{m-1} + Ut^m$
$= (1-\alpha t)(1-\beta t)(1-\gamma t)(1-\delta t)$ etc.

methods.what: Difference of the polynomial at t and u factored by (t-u)
Telescoping expansion of the difference of products of linear factors at t and u
methods.quote:
ist $= (u-t)\alpha(1-\beta t)(1-\gamma t)(1-\delta t) \ldots$
$+ (u-t)\beta(1-\alpha u)(1-\gamma t)(1-\delta t) \ldots$
